title: How to change cursor in Finder on Mac: modify size, outline, and fill color
metaTitle: How to change cursor on Mac: size, color, and accessibility
description: Learn how to change cursor on Mac using System Settings. Follow this guide to adjust your pointer size, outline, and fill color for better visibility.
targetKeyword: how to change cursor on mac
intro: You can change your cursor on a Mac by adjusting its size, outline color, and fill color in System Settings. These changes apply system-wide, including within Finder and all your installed applications.
tldr: Open System Settings from the Apple menu.
Navigate to Accessibility and select Display.
Adjust the Pointer section to change size and colors.
Enable Shake mouse pointer to locate if you lose your cursor often.
Use third-party tools like Mousecape if you need custom cursor icons.

blocks.text: Apple provides native tools to make your cursor easier to see. You can change how to change cursor on Mac by modifying the pointer size and color. These settings are found in the Accessibility menu. They are designed to help users with visual impairments or those working on high-resolution displays. Many users find that a larger cursor helps them work faster on 4K or 5K monitors. You cannot change the actual shape of the cursor to a custom icon using native settings. If you want a different shape, you must look into third-party software. These native tools are reliable and do not impact your system performance.
How to change cursor on Mac: Step by step
Follow these steps to update your pointer appearance on modern versions of macOS.

items: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner.
Select System Settings from the dropdown menu.
Click Accessibility in the left sidebar.
Select Display from the list of options.
Scroll down to find the Pointer section.
Adjust the size slider to your preference.
Click the color wells to change the outline or fill color.

blocks.text: Apple prioritizes stability and security. Allowing users to replace system cursors with custom images could lead to rendering issues. It could also obscure important UI elements. The current settings allow for enough contrast to help most users. If you change the fill color to something bright, use the outline color to keep the edges sharp. A black outline against a yellow fill is a common choice for high visibility. Remember that these settings apply to every app on your Mac. You cannot have a blue cursor in Finder and a red one in Safari. The system treats all pointers as a single global setting.
Common mistakes when changing cursor settings

One common error is choosing a fill color that matches your desktop wallpaper. This makes the cursor hard to see against certain backgrounds. Always test your new colors against both light and dark backgrounds. Another mistake is ignoring the Shake mouse pointer to locate feature. If you frequently lose your cursor, this feature is more effective than just increasing the size. It makes the cursor grow temporarily when you move your mouse quickly. This is often enough to find it without needing a permanent large pointer. If your settings are greyed out, check if you are using a managed Mac. Work or school computers often restrict these changes through mobile device management profiles.

If you really need a custom cursor icon, you might consider tools like Mousecape. These tools allow you to import custom cursor files. They are not supported by Apple and can be difficult to set up. Some users report that they can cause minor graphical glitches. Always read the documentation for these tools before installing them. Most of them are free or offer short trials. Be wary of any tool that asks for full disk access or administrator privileges. Only download software from reputable developers. If you decide to use them, ensure you know how to reset your cursor to the default state. This is usually done by deleting the custom cape or theme within the app.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor shape on Mac?
faq.answer: No, macOS does not natively support changing the cursor icon shape. You can only modify its size, outline color, and fill color.

faq.question: Will these settings change the cursor in all apps?
faq.answer: Yes, these settings are system-wide and will apply to Finder, web browsers, and all other applications.

faq.question: What if I cannot change the cursor settings?
faq.answer: If the options are greyed out, your Mac might be managed by an administrator. Contact your IT department for assistance.
